issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff who is out of possession cannot maintain a suit seeking only a declaration of title without seeking recovery of possession.
material_facts: The trial court found that the Temple had continuously possessed the disputed property and that the plaintiff was not in possession.
The plaintiff sought a declaration and a mandatory injunction concerning revenue records, but did not seek recovery of possession.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not maintainable because the plaintiff, being out of possession, omitted the further relief of recovery of possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 bars a declaration when the plaintiff is able to seek further relief but omits it. The Court relied on Ram Saran and Anr. v. Smt. Ganga Devi, AIR 1972 SC 2685, which held that a suit for declaration alone is not maintainable where the plaintiff is out of possession and has not sought possession.

predicates.civil_property_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit asserting a right in property.
predicates.plaintiff_out_of_possession: The plaintiff was not in possession of the property, and another person was found to possess it.
predicates.only_declaration_and_incidental_relief_s: The plaintiff sought a declaration and an incidental form of relief but did not seek recovery of possession.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff brings a civil property suit, is out of possession, and seeks only a declaration with incidental relief rather than possession, the suit is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court cannot reverse concurrent findings in a second appeal while leaving unaddressed an independent ground on which the lower courts dismissed the suit.
material_facts: The trial court and the first appellate court both dismissed the suit, including on the ground that the plaintiff was out of possession and had not sought recovery of possession.
The High Court decreed the suit without addressing or setting aside that ground.
The High Court exercised jurisdiction in a second appeal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in reversing the lower courts without holding that their ground for finding the suit not maintainable was legally unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court could not reverse the decrees without dealing with the lower courts' reasoning that independently supported dismissal and holding that reasoning legally unsustainable.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding before the High Court was a second appeal.
predicates.concurrent_lower_court_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same result on findings relevant to dismissal of the suit.
predicates.independent_dismissal_ground_left_unaddr: The High Court reversed the dismissal without addressing an independent ground on which the lower courts had relied.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, when the lower courts have made concurrent findings and the High Court leaves an independent dismissal ground unaddressed, its reversal is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: Evidence of a source of title that was not pleaded cannot be relied on to establish title when the opposing party had no opportunity to meet that case.
material_facts: The plaintiff's pleaded case was that the predecessor in title acquired the property by inheritance.
The plaintiff relied on an earlier sale deed to establish a different source of the predecessor's title, although that source had not been pleaded.
The plaintiff admitted that the deed had not been disclosed in the plaint, and the amendment application seeking new pleadings was rejected by the first appellate court.
issues.conclusion: The courts below rightly declined to rely on the unpleaded deed to establish the plaintiff's title.
issues.legal_principle: A party must plead the source of title on which the claim is based. Without that pleading, the opposing party has no opportunity to rebut the case, and evidence concerning the unpleaded source cannot be relied on to establish title. The judgment cites no earlier case for this principle.

predicates.civil_title_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit to establish title to property.
predicates.title_source_not_pleaded: The plaintiff did not plead the source of title later relied on to establish ownership.
predicates.evidence_of_unpleaded_title_source_intro: The plaintiff introduced evidence concerning that unpleaded source of title.

issues.definition: In a civil title suit, evidence of a title source that was not pleaded cannot support the claim when the plaintiff later introduces it.

issues.legal_issue: Instruments describing a parent parcel do not establish title to a specific subdivision when the subdivision already existed and the instruments do not identify it.
material_facts: Revenue records showed that the original survey parcel had been divided into three subdivisions before the transfers relied on by the plaintiff.
The deeds in the plaintiff's chain of title described part of the original parcel but did not identify a subdivision.
The plaintiff later amended the plaint to claim a specific subdivision, but the sale deed in the plaintiff's favour still did not describe that subdivision.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff failed to prove that the deeds in the claimed chain of title concerned the specific subdivision claimed in the suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the requirement that a claimant prove title to the property actually claimed. Where subdivisions already exist, deeds that refer only to the parent parcel do not establish that they concern the particular subdivision claimed. The judgment cites no earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: civil_title_suit and subdivision_existed_before_claimed_transfers and instruments_describe_only_parent_parcel and claim_targets_specific_subdivision

predicates.civil_title_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit to establish title to a specified part of a larger parcel.
predicates.subdivision_existed_before_claimed_trans: The parcel had already been divided into subdivisions before the transfers relied on by the plaintiff.
predicates.instruments_describe_only_parent_parcel: The instruments in the asserted chain of title referred to the parent parcel without identifying a subdivision.
predicates.claim_targets_specific_subdivision: The plaintiff sought a declaration of title to one particular subdivision.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff claims a specific subdivision that existed before the asserted transfers, instruments describing only the parent parcel do not prove title to that subdivision.

issues.legal_issue: A suit is defective for non-joinder when the relief sought extends to property recorded in the name of an owner who has not been joined.
material_facts: The plaintiff admitted that one subdivision was recorded in the name of another owner and that the owner had not been made a party.

The High Court granted relief over the remainder of the original parcel after recognizing that the Temple owned the other subdivisions; that remainder included the subdivision recorded in the absent owner's name.
The trial court and first appellate court had held that the absent owner was a necessary party.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's grant of relief over the subdivision recorded in the absent owner's name was erroneous, and the suit was defective for non-joinder of that necessary party.
issues.legal_principle: A necessary party whose recorded property is affected by the relief must be joined to the suit. The judgment cites no provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.civil_property_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking relief concerning property.
predicates.relief_covers_property_recorded_to_absen: The relief sought extended to property recorded in the name of a person other than the plaintiff or the defendants who were parties.
predicates.recorded_owner_not_joined: The person in whose name the property was recorded was not made a party to the suit.

issues.definition: A civil property suit is defective for non-joinder when the relief sought covers property recorded to an owner who was not joined.
